name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+33 partisan lean makes a Democratic win nearly impossible
Incumbent Robert Aderholt running for reelection with a large financial edge
Challenger Amanda Pusczek raised only about $15,600 with under $500 on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at roughly 98%
model.rationale: The R+33 district, a long-serving incumbent, and a massive fundraising gap leave the Democrat with no realistic path; markets agree at about a 98% Republican win probability. The forecast sits near the fundamentals-based estimate rather than the slightly narrower combined figure.
model.watch: A surprise incumbent scandal or retirement followed by a competitive open-seat primary would be the only realistic opening for Democrats.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwestern Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt has held the seat since 1997 and is running again with about $750,000 on hand after raising more than $1 million. His Democratic challenger, Amanda Pusczek, has raised under $16,000 and had only a few hundred dollars in the bank, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 98%. With no meaningful campaign infrastructure or funding on the Democratic side, the seat is safely in Republican hands this cycle.
